decisions.summary: The code T16's field port leaves dead (plot_texture, the old comb's pending slots, _sharp_corners, _toward, CITY_TIER_SCALES, dead constants, dike_crest, dead names in banks/frame/partition/polder/pockets) is deleted in a later non-phase landing, not in T16's landing.
decisions.why: The GM's approved design says the old implementation is deleted IN THE SAME LANDING (section 3 step 5) and 'A phase is done when the old code is gone. No fallback path, no flag. The landing's size delta shows the deletion.' (section 5 item 5); the spec carries it as FR-005, which the block never cites - it attributes the constraint only to FR-021. Not physically impossible: the deletions can sit in T16's delta, at the cost of the claims FR-021 then owes in those files. Not implied by the GM's words: amendment 6 ('every Rust stage end its initial implementation with zero open claims') lets no old code outlive the landing, and the 2026-10-27 words say the claims work is owed regardless. Applying the rule literally costs work and defeats no stated purpose; the split defeats two (the size delta no longer shows the deletion; the phase counts as landed before its old code is gone). Faithful: the deletions in T16's landing with FR-021's claims closed, or the GM's own words relaxing section 3.5/5.5 - an arbiter ruling is not the GM's words.

decisions.summary: The deletion landing runs under the claims switch's report (feature 445), not FR-021's zero-open-claims refusal.
decisions.why: Derivative of T23-split: FR-021's 'report for every other landing' applies only because the deletion was moved out of the phase landing. The deletion is part of the stage's initial implementation (section 3.5), so holding it at report lets that implementation end with open claims, against amendment 6's 'zero open claims'. Falls with T23-split.

decisions.summary: The deletion list is derived from make dead-closure BASE=<T16's merge base>; each deleted name's tests deleted with it; done when dead-closure lists nothing T16's port left.
decisions.why: The enumeration names its search space (a mechanism, not a name census), and deleting tests with their code keeps the coverage floor; serves section 5.5's 'old code gone'. Note the class seam: 'water_frame.rs reaching the shared counts.rs' is water_frame's leftover, not code T16's port left dead, and the block's single justification does not cover it; it is within only as dead-code removal under section 5.5 for water_frame.

decisions.summary: Re-price the dry hem, the hem's laid plots, the outline by bands and the hem's registry share on fan_middle's odds at the field derivation's next re-derivation, not now.
decisions.why: The GM accepted the derivation as it reads at 1.9x, 'even if our original estimate was a bit off because of failing to count/consider/calculate everything' (444#6); deferring the re-pricing to the next re-derivation leaves that accepted derivation unedited and serves S7 and FR-014 (the typical case) when it happens.

decisions.summary: Name the cleared-middle band (fan_middle laying one band along the whole canal) in the field contract's Writes.
decisions.why: Records in the contract what the stage writes, sourced to 0011's drawing page (FR-015: the contract written from the research record).

decisions.summary: The same re-derivation prices the dry plots' furrow rows (pt_test@furrows) and the copy to the Python stages (write@py_export), which goes as those stages port.
decisions.why: Counting what was uncounted is S5/S7; the GM's 444#6 answer names the miss ('failing to count/consider/calculate everything').

decisions.summary: The field's budget stands at 1.9 per thing of the derivation (118,739 at 40, 218,411 at 80).
decisions.why: The GM's words verbatim, 444#6 option (a). Within ONLY with the pinned figures fixed: the block defines the budget as 1.9x the derivation and then plans to grow the derivation, without saying the pin stays at 118,739/218,411. If the pin scales with the re-derivation, that is a raise without the GM's words (section 5 item 4, FR-015's make budget-change).

decisions.summary: Green exit: a MODE BUDGET verdict on the re-priced rows; done when the hem rows' expected plots at 40 sit within the measured mean's band.
decisions.why: Measured against the typical case (FR-014). Note the inconsistency: constraint 2 cites FR-013 ('a figure change re-owes a ruling'), but the green exit names only a MODE BUDGET verdict and no make arbiter-ask; if the field's pin rests on an accept, FR-013's ruling is owed too.
